certificate.title: Start Adopting AI in Your Accounting Practice Completion

course.description: Go from "I know I should use AI" to actually using it daily — with a practical, low-risk approach any accountant can follow. Based on Brock Beyer's advice for accountants who haven't started yet.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Start Adopting AI in Your Accounting Practice.

activities.title: Just Start — Pick Any AI Tool and Open It

lessons.content: Don't overthink the tool choice. Open Claude, ChatGPT, or any LLM. The biggest barrier isn't picking the right tool — it's not starting at all. Open a free account and type your first question today.
lessons.title: Just Start — Pick Any AI Tool and Open It

activities.title: Ask the AI a Real Accounting Question

lessons.content: Instead of searching Stack Exchange or the FASB codification, ask the AI. Try something like: "What's the correct treatment for a prepaid expense that spans two fiscal years?" Compare the answer to what you know. This builds trust (or healthy skepticism).
lessons.title: Ask the AI a Real Accounting Question

activities.title: Fail Fast, Fail Early — Learn from Mistakes

lessons.content: Your first AI outputs will have errors. That's expected. The goal is to learn what it gets right, what it gets wrong, and how to refine your prompts. Each mistake teaches you how to work with the tool more effectively.
lessons.title: Fail Fast, Fail Early — Learn from Mistakes

activities.title: Apply the Rules-Based vs. Judgment-Based Filter

lessons.content: Before automating anything, ask: "Is this task rules-based or does it require professional judgment?" Rules-based tasks (data entry, categorization, reconciliation) are ideal for AI. Judgment-heavy tasks (materiality decisions, going concern assessments) should stay human — use AI as a thought partner, not the decision-maker.
lessons.title: Apply the Rules-Based vs. Judgment-Based Filter

activities.title: When You're Stuck, Ask the AI for Help with AI

lessons.content: Meta, but powerful. If you don't know how to prompt effectively, ask: "I'm an accountant trying to use AI to automate [task]. Can you help me write a good prompt for this?" The AI will coach you on how to use it better.
lessons.title: When You're Stuck, Ask the AI for Help with AI

lessons.content: Not everything should be AI-generated. Client communications, advisory conversations, and relationship-building should retain your voice. Use AI for the grunt work so you have more time for the human work.
lessons.title: Keep Authenticity Where It Matters
